function: Learned likelihood estimation of received samples for Viterbi sequence detection/decoding of single-carrier ISI links, robust to non-Gaussian interference and unknown CSI (pp. 1, 4).
system: Main link SISO ISI (BPSK, QPSK, 16QAM, BLE GFSK); SIMO extension with one transmit and two receive antennas; no RIS; band not stated (pp. 3, 6, 9).
method: Quasi-neural network (one hidden layer, Gaussian-mixture activation, weights tied to channel parameters) trained per packet by backpropagation on a short labelled pilot, cross-entropy, feeding Viterbi (pp. 4-5).
data_channel: Simulated ISI channels (L=2 to 4) with BPSK, QPSK, 16QAM, GFSK; Gaussian, Cauchy, Laplace noise or BPSK interference; no standard channel model, dataset or measurement (pp. 7-9).
test_conditions: Trained on the pilot of each packet (16 to 1024 symbols), tested on the data of that packet; architecture mismatch with channel length L tested (pp. 5, 7-8).
baselines: Non-learned: conventional Viterbi with perfect CSI, MMSE equalizer (SIMO). Learned: OLTD [21] (online learning trellis diagram) (pp. 7-10).
metrics: Bit error rate versus SNR, pilot length, and noise scale; learnable variables and complexity order (pp. 6-9).
complexity: Training complexity O(K1(L+1+Q)) with L+1+Q learnable variables, versus OLTD O(K1(200|X|^L)) and ViterbiNet O(K1(5000|X|^L)) in Table I (pp. 6-7).
q1_support: p. 7: "we consider transmitting BPSK signals via an ISI channel with L = 2"; p. 9: GFSK with "a two-length ISI channel"; custom ISI links, and no 3GPP, COST, DeepMIMO or measured channel is used.
q2_support: p. 5: "K1 and K2 denote the pilot length and data length", so the QNN is trained on the pilot of each packet and tested on that packet; pp. 8-9: only architecture-versus-channel-length mismatch, still trained on the pilot of the actual channel.
q3_support: p. 7: "the QNN-decoder only requires around 64 pilots for accurate training, while the OLTD needs around 256 pilots" (BER 1.5e-3, learned OLTD [21]); Figs. 6-9 BER versus conventional Viterbi; p. 9: "achieves around 3.5dB gains compared with the MMSE".
q4_support: p. 6: "The computational complexity of the QNN for training is O(K1 (L + 1 + Q))"; Table I (p. 7) lists complexity and learnable variables for OLTD, ViterbiNet and QNN.
q5_support: p. 6: "we evaluate the performance of the QNN-decoder for single-carrier communications with an ISI channel"; results come from the authors' own simulation, and no code or data link, DOI or availability statement appears in the paper.
notes: Borderline for the system rule: the main link is SISO (p. 3, Figs. 6-11) and the abstract calls multi-antenna an extension (p. 1), but a stated contribution (p. 2) and Sec. IV and V-C evaluate SIMO with 1 transmit and 2 receive antennas (Figs. 12-13), so the link is not single-antenna throughout; included, reviewer to confirm. If the rule is read on the main link, exclude with reason system. QNN weights are tied to physical parameters but trained by backpropagation on pilots, so counted as learned. ViterbiNet appears only in the complexity table. Tables I-II read from the PDF image (p. 7). BLE GFSK is a standard modulation but its channel is a custom ISI model, so q1 is 0.
